directAnswer: USB-C issues can stem from incompatible cables, faulty ports, or device settings. Ensure that both the cable and device support the same USB-C specifications.
summary: USB-C not working can be caused by various factors including hardware compatibility and settings. Troubleshooting steps can help identify the issue.

sections.heading: Check Cable Compatibility
sections.body: Ensure that the USB-C cable you are using is compatible with your device. Some cables only support charging, while others support data transfer and video output.

sections.heading: Inspect the USB-C Port
sections.body: Check for any debris or damage in the USB-C port on both the device and the cable. A clean, undamaged port is essential for proper connection.

sections.heading: Review Device Settings
sections.body: On some devices, USB settings may need to be adjusted. For example, on Android devices, you may need to select the USB mode (e.g., File Transfer) after connecting.

steps.title: Test with a Different Cable
steps.detail: Try using a different USB-C cable that is known to work with other devices. This can help determine if the original cable is faulty.

steps.title: Try a Different Port
steps.detail: If your device has multiple USB-C ports, try connecting to a different port to see if the issue persists.

steps.title: Restart Your Device
steps.detail: Sometimes, a simple restart can resolve connectivity issues. Restart your device and try the connection again.

faqs.question: What should I do if my USB-C device is not charging?
faqs.answer: Ensure that the charger is compatible with your device and that the cable is functioning properly. Also, check if the power source is working.

faqs.question: Can I use a USB-C hub with my device?
faqs.answer: Yes, but ensure that the hub is compatible with your device's specifications to avoid connectivity issues.

faqs.question: Why does my USB-C port only charge and not transfer data?
faqs.answer: This may be due to the cable being designed only for charging or the device's USB settings not being configured for data transfer.

caveats: Different devices may have unique USB-C implementations, so troubleshooting steps may vary.
